paper.title_en: Dual-horizon Topological Thermodynamics of a Kerr-Newman-de Sitter Black Hole in Bumblebee Gravity
paper.abstract_en: This work is devoted to study the topological classification of a Kerr-Newman-de Sitter (KNdS) black hole (BH) in bumblebee gravity (BBG) subject to changes in various parameters. Based on generalized free energy techniques coupled with Duan's $\phi $ mapping topological current theory, we find that BH can be separated into different topological classes. Interestingly, our result demonstrates that the existence of a number of horizons in dS spacetime, in particular, we find that both the event horizon and the cosmological horizon carry two zero points with opposite winding numbers, so that each horizon has vanishing total topological number, $W_h=W_c=0$. The winding-number assignment of the two cosmological-horizon defects is reversed relative to the event horizon, and this classification is unchanged by the electric charge Q and the Lorentz-violation parameter L.
